body.p: allows you to customize certain aspects of built-in or custom document templates. For example, you can customize the icons or specify a prefix/suffix that will be used for the proposed file name in the New document wizardNew from templates wizard.

section.title: Template Properties File Reference
section.p: Each document, archive, or project template can have a sibling .properties file with the same base name as the template file (for example, Concept.dita and Concept.properties). The properties file configures how the template is displayed and behaves in the New document wizardNew from templates wizard and in other new-document dialog boxes.
You can add comments in a properties file by starting a line with #. Comment lines are ignored when the file is read.
The following table lists all supported properties:

section.p: The following example shows a typical properties file for a custom DITA topic template:
section.codeblock:
# Icons (paths relative to the template file) smallIcon=../icons/MyTopic_16.png bigIcon=../icons/MyTopic_48.png
# Required for DITA topic/map templates type=dita
# Optional display name and file-name defaults displayName=My Custom Topic # filenamePrefix=prod_ # filenameSuffix=_draft
# Tooltip description (external HTML file, not inline text) longDescriptionReference=../descriptions/MyTopic.html
# Optional tag; use "popular" to also show the template in the Popular category tags=advanced
section.note: To change the category path for an entire templates subfolder, create category.properties in that folder (not next to an individual template) with a line such as categoryPath=My Company/DITA/Topics.

section.title: How to Customize the Icons for a Document Template
section.p:
If you want to customize the icons to be used for document templates, use a properties file to specify the icons using the following procedure:
Create a new properties file or edit an existing one following these guidelines:
If you want to create a new properties file, you can use the Properties template found in the New Document folder in the New document wizardNew from templates wizard. If you want to edit an existing template, you can find them within the subfolders in the templates folder for each framework (for example, the DITA topic properties file is located in: OXYGEN_INSTALL_DIR/frameworks/dita/templates/topic/topic.properties).
Use the same name as your custom template file except with a .properties extension (for example, MyTemplate.properties).
In this properties file, specify the paths to the icons that will be used in the new file wizard. The properties file should look like this:type=general smallIcon=../icons/Article_16.png bigIcon=../icons/Article_48.pngFor DITA files, the type property must be set to dita. Otherwise, the template will not appear in the dialog box for creating new DITA topics from the DITA Maps Manager. For all other types of files, set it to general. The icons specified in this properties file will only be used for the new file wizards and not in any other part of the interface. Use PNG or GIF images (a size of 16×16 pixels is recommended for smallIcon and 48×48 pixels for bigIcon). For a complete list of properties, see Template Properties File Reference.If you created a new template and chose to use a custom directory for the new template (in step 2 of the new template procedure), make sure that the path to the icons is relative to that directory.
Save the properties file in the same directory as your custom template.
Open the new file wizard ( File New
File New New from Templates ) and you should see your custom icons next to the document template in the appropriate folder.

section.title: How to Add a Prefix or Suffix to File Names for a Document Template
section.p:
You can use a properties file for each document template to add a prefix or suffix to the file name that is proposed in certain dialog boxes when you create a new file from that template. This applies to the following new document dialog boxes:
The new document dialog box that appears when you click the New button on the toolbar (or File New ). The prefix or suffix is added to the name of the file in the Save as field.
The new document dialog box that appears when you click the New button on the toolbar (or File New Other
). The prefix or suffix is added to the name of the file in the File field.
The new document dialog box that appears when you select New File from the contextual menu in the Project view. The prefix or suffix is added to the name of the file in the File name field.
The new document dialog box that appears when you select New New from Templates [Template Name] Next from the contextual menu in the Project Explorer view. The prefix or suffix is added to the name of the file in the File field.
For DITA files, it also applies to the new document dialog box that appears when you select Append Child New , Insert Before New , or Insert After New from the DITA Maps Manager. The prefix or suffix is added to the name of the file in the Save as field.
For DITA files, it also applies to the Fast Create Topics dialog box that you can use to create multiple skeleton topics at once.

To add a prefix or suffix to the file names for a document template, follow these steps:
Create a new properties file or edit an existing one.
If you create a new properties file, use the same name as the template file except with a .properties extension (for example, MyTemplate.properties). This properties file specifies the prefix/suffix that will be used to propose the file name in the new file wizards.
When defining the prefix/suffix, the properties file should look something like this:type=general filenamePrefix=prod_ filenameSuffix=_test
For DITA files, the type property must be set to dita. For all other types of files, set it to general.
If you edit an existing template, simply define the prefix/suffix as specified above.
Save the properties file in the same directory as the document template.
Open the new document wizard (using the methods described above) and when you select the appropriate template, you should see your prefix or suffix in the file name that is proposed in that dialog box.
section.note: The filenamePrefix and filenameSuffix properties can also have editor variables that do not require user interaction (i.e. editor variables that have ${ask()} and ${answer()} as values cannot be used).

section.title: How to Configure the Displayed Names for Document Templates
section.p:
To change the name that is displayed for a document template, use the following procedure:
Create a new properties file or edit an existing one. If you create a new properties file, use the same name as the template file except with a .properties extension (for example, MyTemplate.properties).
Add a displayName property in the properties file:displayName=My Template Name
The names for framework-specific document templates (such as DITA Topic or DocBook Article, as you would see in the Framework templates folder in the New file wizard) can be translated via the internationalization support. In this case, the properties file should contain something like:displayName=${i18n(tag)}
where tag refers to an entry in the translation.xml file for that specific framework (for example, OXYGEN_INSTALL_DIR/frameworks/dita/i18n/translation.xml for DITA).
Save the properties file in the same directory as the document template.
Open the new file wizard ( File New
File New New from Templates ) and you should see the new name for the template.

section.title: How to Add a Long Description (Tooltip) for a Document Template
section.p: You can provide additional information about a template that is shown as a tooltip when users hover over the template in the New document wizardNew document wizard. The description is stored in a separate HTML file and referenced from the properties file using the longDescriptionReference property. You cannot write the description text directly in the .properties file.

To add a long description for a document template, follow these steps: Create an HTML file that contains the description. A simple HTML fragment is sufficient, for example:

The DITA Concept topic type provides conceptual information to support the performance of tasks.

Store the file in a folder that is easy to reference from the template (for example, a descriptions subfolder next to your templates folder). In the sibling .properties file for the template, add the longDescriptionReference property pointing to the HTML file:type=dita longDescriptionReference=../descriptions/MyTopic.html Open the New document wizard, hover over the template, and verify that the tooltip shows the HTML content.
section.note: Built-in DITA templates use this mechanism. For example, OXYGEN_INSTALL_DIR/frameworks/dita/templates/topic/Concept.properties references ../descriptions/topic/Concept.html.

section.title: How to Customize the Category Path for Templates
section.p: By default, templates are grouped in the New document wizardNew document wizard according to the physical folder structure under the framework's templates directory. You can override the displayed category path for an entire templates subfolder by creating a category.properties file in that folder.

To customize the category path:
In the templates subfolder whose category you want to customize, create a file named category.properties.
Add the categoryPath property with the desired path, using slashes as separators:categoryPath=DITA/Topics
For example, built-in DITA topic templates use OXYGEN_INSTALL_DIR/frameworks/dita/templates/topic/category.properties with categoryPath=DITA/Topics, so the templates appear under DITA > Topics regardless of the physical folder name.
Open the New wizard and verify that the templates from that folder appear under the new category path.

section.title: How to Add Placeholders or Hints in a Document Template
section.p: If a document template contains empty elements, it may not be clear to the Author what should be inserted in them. You can define placeholders in document templates that provide hints for Authors to help them understand what type of content should be added in any particular empty element within the document. The placeholder text is specified using a processing instruction and the placeholders are removed when the Author inserts content in the corresponding element.

To define placeholders in a document template to provide authors with hints, follow this procedure: Edit the document template. Add placeholders in the form of processing instructions within the elements where you want hints to be displayed when an Author creates a document from the template. For example: <?oxy-placeholder content="Enter a title"?>

The elements that contain the placeholder processing instructions cannot contain other content/text, not even whitespace used for indentation. Otherwise, the placeholder will not be rendered properly. Save the template file. Use the New document wizardNew from templates wizard to create a new document using your customized template and you should see the hints in the open document.

section.title: How to Add a Template in the Popular Category of the New Document Wizard
section.p: The New document wizardNew document wizard contains a Popular category that includes many of the most common new document templates for various built-in document types (frameworks). It is possible to add more templates to this Popular category.

The templates in this category are marked as popular using a properties file that contains popular as one of the values for the tags property. For example, for the OXYGEN_INSTALL_DIR/frameworks/dita/templates/topic/Topic.dita template, there is a Topic.properties sibling file that contains tags=popular,advanced.

To add another template to the Popular category, create/edit the sibling properties file for the particular template and include popular in the tags property (for example, tags=popular or tags=popular,advanced). For details about all supported properties, see Template Properties File Reference.

section.title: Resources
section.p: To see a visual demonstration of how to customize document templates and to get more ideas for other advanced customization possibilities, watch our Webinar: Working with DITA in Oxygen - Customizing the Editing Experience.
